title: Alexanderplatz History - Quick Summary
items: **Named in 1805** after Tsar Alexander I. Before that it was the Ochsenmarkt, a cattle market and parade ground.
**The railway made it busy:** the Stadtbahn viaduct and the station opened in 1882.
**The Berolina** stood here from 1895, a 7.5-metre copper statue of the city. She was dismantled in the war and never came back.
**The oldest buildings on the square** are Peter Behrens's Alexanderhaus and Berolinahaus, built 1929 to 1932.
**April 1945:** the fighting destroyed most of the old square.
**The GDR rebuilt it** after a 1964 competition: TV Tower and World Clock in 1969, the fountain and the big blocks around 1970.
**4 November 1989:** hundreds of thousands demonstrated here, five days before the Wall opened.
**See it in 30 minutes:** World Clock, Behrens houses, fountain, Haus des Lehrers mural, TV Tower.
